title: The Oath-Warden
openingText: Munn keeps the boundary-stones, and she has been keeping them since before the current barons held the manors. 'You have been near the oath-stones,' she says. It is not an accusation yet. 'I would rather hear what you did there from you than from a levyman with a headache.'
dialogueCordial: Then we want the same thing, and I have been alone in wanting it for some while.
dialogueStrained: I hear you. I have heard a great many reasonable men explain the downs to me.
dialogueHostile: Do not mistake my patience for weakness. I have outlasted four barons.
dialogueWalkaway: Go on, then. The stones will still be here, and so will I.
dialogueAccept: Then it is agreed, and I will hold you to it, and you will find I am very good at holding.

terms.description: Munn's writ: safe passage through every manor in the downs, honoured on sight.
She teaches you what the charm-work on the stones actually binds, and to whom.
You undertake to break no further oath-stone in the Amber Downs.
Her wardens are hungry. Fifteen supplies, and she will not ask twice.
This is not a negotiation. It is an interview, and she has already decided.
